predecessors.note: Infobox: independence from the Ilkhanate 1337, predecessor Ilkhanate. The Ilkhanate dossier lists the Sarbadars as a successor with Cliopatria's 1344 shape.

successors.note: Infobox: successors Timurid Empire and the Kurtid dynasty. 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad submitted to Timur at Nishapur in 1381 and was confirmed as governor of Sabzevar; Timur never garrisoned Sabzevar.

capitals.name: Sabzevar
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Sabzevar. 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad captured Sabzevar c. 1361 and Shiraz-based dervishes took it c. 1376; no other seat is named.

rulers.name: 'Abd al-Razzaq
rulers.note: The list gives 1332-1338, but the body dates the revolt to early 1337 and Sabzevar's capture to summer 1337. The list 'conflicts with some of the body text and with the separate dynasty table', so treat its dates as approximate.

rulers.name: Wajih ad-Din Mas'ud
rulers.note: The body has Mas'ud captured and executed in 1344.

rulers.name: Yahya Karabi
rulers.note: The body: Yahya Karawi submitted to Togha Temur in 1351/52 and struck him down in 1353.

rulers.name: Khwaja 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad, restored
rulers.note: Died 1386 of wounds from Timur's Lesser Luristan campaign.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the state 'emerged around early 1337 under 'Abd al-Razzaq ... after he led a revolt in Bashtin, a district of Sabzevar'; Sabzevar was taken in summer 1337. Cliopatria starts in 1344.

correction.text: the 1340-1343 holdings: Nishapur, Jajarm, Damghan, Simnan and Gurgan beside the Sabzevar core

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 1340 Mas'ud pushed the Ja'un-i Qurban out of Nishapur and took Jajarm, Damghan, Simnan and Gurgan after Togha Temur's forces were destroyed (the last four undated). Cliopatria's 1344 shape (418,562 km2: Golestan, Mazandaran, North Khorasan, Semnan, half of Tehran and Razavi Khorasan, and Turkmen land) is this high-water mark, which the page says was lost in 1344.

418,562 km2 for 1344-1351 is the 1340-43 maximum; the page: 'Mas'ud's campaign against Togha Temur failed. He was captured and executed, and most conquests were lost. Remaining holdings were the Sabzevar region and possibly Juvayn and Nishapur.' The page gives no area. Correction: the Sabzevar core and Nishapur (Juvayn lies inside the radius).

correction.text: Sabzevar, Nishapur and Tus, for 1354-1362 (the core alone in 1352)

keyframe_review.note: 418,417 km2. 1352 stands as the core of 1344-1351 (Yahya Karawi submitted to Togha Temur in 1351/52); 1353 is the new keyframe sarbadars_1353; from 1354 the pages leave Sabzevar, Nishapur and Tus as the Sarbadar land (Muluk Sabzavari 'joined the revolt in Tus' in 1389).

correction.text: the core plus the Ray area, Tus and Astarabad

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Togha Temur was killed near Astarabad in 1353 'the Sarbadars then gained the Ray area, Tus, Astarabad, and Shasman' (Shasman not in the gazetteer, left out).

418,190 km2 for 1363-1374. The page has 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad ruling from 1364 (captured Sabzevar c. 1361), Astarabad 'temporarily retaken' 1365/6-1368/9 and a failed Sarbadar-backed revolt in Kirman 1373-74; none of it reaches the plateau of the shape. Correction: Sabzevar, Nishapur and Tus; Astarabad only 1366-1369 (ledger).

correction.text: Sabzevar and Tus without Nishapur from 1376

keyframe_review.note: 398,520 km2. About 1376 the Kartids took Nishapur and Shiraz-based dervishes took Sabzevar (the list has Rukn ad-Din for 1376-1379); correction removes Nishapur for 1376-1384.

correction.text: Sabzevar and Tus under Timur's governor 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad, to 1386

keyframe_review.note: 398,123 km2. 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad submitted to Timur in 1381 at Nishapur and remained governor of Sabzevar until his death in 1386; the dossier ends in 1386 although Cliopatria runs to 1394 (Muluk Sabzavari revolting in Tus in 1389 and Khwaja Mas'ud Sabzavari holding Baghdad for Timur in 1393-94 are individuals under Timur).

ledger.note: 1337: 'Abd al-Razzaq's revolt in Bashtin, a district of Sabzevar, founds the Sarbadar state ('independence from the Ilkhanate 1337'); Sabzevar is taken in summer 1337.
Summer 1337: Sabzevar is taken ('Sabzevar was taken in summer 1337').
1340: Mas'ud pushes the Ja'un-i Qurban out; Arghun Shah gives up Nishapur and withdraws to Tus ('Mas'ud pushed out the Ja'un-i Qurban under Arghun Shah, who gave up Nishapur and withdrew to Tus').
1340 and after: the Sarbadars take Jajarm, Damghan, Simnan and Gurgan 'after Togha Temur's forces were destroyed' (the page gives 1340 for the sequence and no exact date for these four).

1344: Mas'ud's campaign against Togha Temur fails; he is captured and executed and most conquests are lost; the Bavandids trapped the Sarbadar army (Togha Temur page). Holdings left: the Sabzevar region and possibly Juvayn and Nishapur.

region.text: the Ray area, Tus, Astarabad (Shasman not in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 1353: Togha Temur is killed near Astarabad (November or December, Togha Temur page); 'the Sarbadars then gained the Ray area, Tus, Astarabad, and Shasman'.

Page silent on how long the 1353 gains lasted: after Togha Temur's death Amir Vali, son of the governor Shaykh-'Ali Hindu, 'seized power' in Astarabad (Togha Temur page, undated) and the Sarbadar page has Astarabad 'temporarily retaken' in 1365/6, so it had been lost; the Ray area is not mentioned again. Bridged at 1354.
1365/6: Astarabad is temporarily retaken by the Sarbadars ('Astarabad was temporarily retaken', 1365/6-1368/9).
1368/9: Astarabad is lost again (the end of 'temporarily retaken', 1365/6-1368/9).
About 1376: Pir 'Ali's Karts take Nishapur ('seizing the city of Nishapur around 1375 or 1376').

1386: 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad dies of wounds from Timur's Lesser Luristan campaign, the last ruler of the page's list; he had submitted to Timur at Nishapur in 1381 and Timur never garrisoned Sabzevar. The page gives no end year and describes the Sarbadars declining after Timur's death; 1386 is my choice, Cliopatria runs to 1394.

wars.name: Sarbadar war with Togha Temur and Arghun Shah
wars.outcome: Mas'ud takes Nishapur, Jajarm, Damghan, Simnan and Gurgan in 1340; his 1344 campaign fails, he is executed and most conquests are lost.
wars.note: Togha Temur page: the Sarbadars killed Shaykh-'Ali Ke'un in May 1343 and 'took much of Khurasan'.

wars.name: Battle of Zava (Sarbadars and Kartids)
wars.outcome: The Karts and Sarbadars met at the Battle of Zava on 18 July 1342; the Kartids survived. No frontier changed.

wars.name: Murder of Togha Temur and the Sarbadar seizure of his lands
wars.outcome: Yahya Karawi and a group of Sarbadars kill Togha Temur in his camp in November or December 1353; much of his territory returns to Sarbadar hands.

wars.name: Sarbadar-Muzaffarid conflicts
wars.outcome: 'Ali backs a revolt in Kirman against Shah Shuja (1373-74), which fails in December 1374; Shah Mansur sides with Amir Vali against 'Ali in 1381. No frontier changed.

wars.name: Timur's takeover of Khorasan
wars.outcome: 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad submits to Timur at Nishapur in 1381 and is confirmed as governor of Sabzevar; he stays loyal until his death in 1386.

certainty.note: A small state of towns on the Khorasan road, ruled by a dozen shifting viziers; the pages name cities, never frontiers. Rule 9: all borders approximate.

notes:
Three pages cited (state article, Togha Temur, Kart dynasty); page budget up to 5, the other two were not needed because the Sarbadars page names every dated event.
Cliopatria problems: (1) All five shapes (418,562 down to 398,123 km2: Golestan, Mazandaran, North Khorasan, Semnan, half of Tehran and Razavi Khorasan, and Turkmen land) are one and the same 1340-43 maximum; the page has most of those conquests lost in 1344, the holdings reduced to Sabzevar, probably Nishapur, and later Tus. (2) The state is dated from 1337 (independence), not 1344. (3) The end: the page's ruler list ends in 1386, Cliopatria in 1394; the page gives no end year. The dossier uses 1386. (4) The page gives no area.
Page disagreements: the infobox start of 'Abd al-Razzaq 1332 is not in the body (early 1337); the ruler list's dates conflict with the body (Mas'ud executed 1344, list 1343) and the list has a gap 1356-1358; the body calls the system an oligarchy or republic, the infobox 'Absolute Monarchy'. 
Not drawn: vassal relations in which the Sarbadars are the vassal (Ilkhanid Togha Temur 1351/52-1353 with tribute; the Chobanid Hasan Kucek and his puppet khan after 1340; Timur 1381-1386); the overlords' dossiers carry them (no Cliopatria relation exists). The Sarbadars of Samarkand (resisting Ilyas Khoja in 1365) are a different group the page mentions without territory. The Mazandaran dervish state of Mir-i Buzurg (destroyed by Timur in 1392) is not mentioned with dates enough to draw.
Counterparts needing dossiers: Togha Temur's khanate in Astarabad, Mazandaran and Gurgan (1339-1353, a puppet Ilkhan; group ia-02 or me-09-x); Amir Vali of Astarabad (c. 1353-1384, expelled by Timur in 1384); the Ja'un-i Qurban of Arghun Shah (to 1340). The Kartid dossier (kartids) has the matching gain of Nishapur in 1376.
Gazetteer: every name resolves; 'Shasman' (district named on the page) is not in the gazetteer and was left out of the regions.
